slides.title: Sliding window and divide and conquer
slides.main: Window: consecutive chunks in one pass; divide and conquer: independent halves and a merge.

captions: Sliding window: consecutive chunks in one pass
Divide and conquer: independent halves, merged answer
Recognize the problem by its wording and pick the pattern

body.text: Fourteen exercises: from anagrams to the segment tree.

slides.title: The window idea
slides.sub: Two boundaries and the state between them
slides.main: Each element enters the window once and leaves once: linear time.

captions: The window is the span between the left and right boundaries
The right boundary widens the window: a new element enters
The left one shrinks the window: an old element leaves
Each element enters and leaves at most once: linear time

frames.text: total: n in + n out = 2n moves

slides.title: Fixed-size window
slides.main: Add the entering element, subtract the leaving one: window sum in O(1).

captions: k = 3: the first window's sum is computed directly
The window slides: add the entering element, subtract the leaving one, one operation
The new window is better: the best answer updated
Updating the state on a slide is constant; best sum 9

slides.title: Variable-size window
slides.main: The right boundary expands, the left shrinks while the window is invalid.

captions: The right boundary adds characters while the window has no repeats
The new “a” is already in the window: the window is invalid
The left boundary drops characters until the repeat is gone
Work is linear: the boundaries move at most 2n times in total

frames.text: left boundary shrank the window to “bca”
max 3: each letter entered and left once

slides.title: Monotonicity
slides.sub: When shrinking the left boundary is correct
slides.main: Expanding must change validity predictably: a sum of positives only grows.

captions: We need the shortest chunk with sum at least 7 (all numbers positive)
The sum fell below the target: expand the right boundary
Target reached: record the length and shrink
Monotonicity: expanding only increases the sum; answer 2

slides.title: Window and frequencies
slides.main: Character counters update in constant time on a slide.

captions: A window as wide as the pattern “abc”; inside are letter counters
Slide: one letter entered, another left, counters updated in constant time
Counters do not match the pattern
One pass over the string; result: positions 0 and 6

frames.text: cba: a1 b1 c1 = abc ✓, anagram at position 0
bae: no c, extra e: no match

slides.title: Monotonic queue
slides.main: Drop from the tail those that can never be the maximum: O(n).

captions: Max in every window of 3: the queue holds decreasing values, the head is the max
A new element smaller than the tail just joins the end
A bigger new element pops all smaller ones from the tail: they can no longer be the answer
The head is the max; indices that left the window are removed from the head
Each element enters and leaves once: O(n)

slides.title: Where the window fails
slides.main: For sums with negatives: prefix sums and a hash table.

captions: All numbers positive: the window sum grows on expanding and falls on shrinking
Negatives present: the sum jumps, so the “shrink left” rule loses its meaning
For sums with negatives use prefix sums and a hash table

slides.title: Divide and conquer
slides.main: Subproblems must be independent; if they overlap, memory is needed (DP).

captions: A problem of size n
Split into independent subproblems of the same kind
Solve small ones directly (or the same way, recursively)
Combine the solutions into the answer. Subproblems must not overlap

slides.title: Time estimate
slides.main: Two halves and a linear merge give n log n; one subproblem gives log n.

captions: Recursion tree: the number of levels is a logarithm
At each level the total merge work is about n
log n levels of n each: n log n in total
One subproblem (binary search): only log n; two halves with a constant merge: n

slides.title: Inversions
slides.main: The right half overtaking the left gives inversions: n log n instead of n².

captions: An inversion is a pair where the left element is greater than the right
A right-half element overtakes all remaining on the left: each overtake is an inversion
We count along with the merge, enumerating nothing
n log n instead of n²: 7 inversions

frames.text: 1 from right: the whole left (3 elements) is greater → +3
2 from left; 3 from right: 5, 6 on the left are greater → +2

slides.title: Fast exponentiation
slides.main: The exponent halves at each step: O(log n) multiplications.

captions: Raise x to the power 13
x¹³ = x · (x⁶)²: compute x⁶ just once
x⁶ = (x³)², x³ = x · (x¹)²: the exponent halves
Reached zero: the depth is a logarithm
5 multiplications instead of 12; for power 1000, about fifteen instead of a thousand

slides.title: Segment tree
slides.main: Query and update in logarithmic time: a path through chunk nodes.

captions: Each node holds the sum of its chunk; leaves are the original array
The sum on [1, 6] is assembled from 4 ready nodes: 3 + 8 + 10 + 2 = 23
Change an element: only the nodes on the path to the root are recomputed
Query and update take a logarithmic number of nodes

slides.title: Recognizing the pattern
slides.sub: The wording hints at the technique
slides.main: Extend the “wording → technique” table as you solve problems.

captions: Consecutive chunks: a window; the property must be monotonic
Max or min among the last k: a monotonic queue
Independent halves and a merge: divide and conquer
Many queries and updates on ranges: a segment tree

slides.title: Summary and practice
slides.main: Monotonicity for the window, independence for divide and conquer.

captions: Window state updates in constant time, the property is monotonic
Drop those that can never be the answer
Two halves and a linear merge give n log n
Range queries and updates in logarithmic time
